name: Malefic Blue-Eyes White Dragon (Retro Formats)
desc: This card cannot be Normal Summoned or Set. This card can only be Special Summoned by removing from play 1 "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from your Deck. There can only be 1 face-up "Malefic" monster on the field. Other monsters you control cannot declare an attack. If there is no face-up Field Spell Card on the field, destroy this card.

cdb_provenance.detail: type, atk, def, level, race, attribute and setcode are copied from the row for the modern card (9433350) in cards.cdb at the ignis-babelcdb revision pinned in data/sources.json. They are NOT independently checked against a period printing: a stat change between the period card and the modern one would not be reproduced. category (a client search filter, not gameplay) is left 0 rather than copied. ot is 8 (SCOPE_ILLEGAL) as for every historical-implementation row upstream.

authorship.note: Written from the record's period text and the ocgcore Lua API, not derived from any Project Ignis CardScripts file, whose licence is AGPL-3.0-or-later (ProjectIgnis/CardScripts COPYING at the ignis-cardscripts pin). Round 031: no Project Ignis card script was opened while writing it; constant.lua and utility.lua (the engine's shared API) were read, and the modern card's behaviour was only observed by running it in the engine harness. A derived script would need an owner licensing decision.

not_reproduced: The period text names no zone for the Special Summon. The script allows it only from the hand, banishing "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from the Deck; a Special Summon from the Deck or another zone by the procedure is not reproduced.
"Malefic" is the archetype code carried by the pinned BabelCDB row, not a period ruling; which cards counted as "Malefic" in 2010 is not modelled.

"There can only be 1 face-up \"Malefic\" monster on the field" uses the engine's unique-on-field check, which counts face-up cards only, as the period text says. The modern card's script behaves the same way in the engine for a face-down Malefic, so that part of the period text is not an observed difference; a second face-up Malefic on the field being destroyed when this card is Special Summoned is tested against the modern card.

The self-destruction with no face-up Field Spell Card is a continuous effect checked against both players' Field Zones; its timing relative to the Special Summon (the card is destroyed at once if no such Field Spell exists) is not established by the record's sources.
"Blue-Eyes White Dragon" is identified by its canonical code (its alternate-art codes alias to it).
The card row's statline is copied from the modern row and not checked against the period printing.
